properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-20: *"just as reflow2 checks that a capability had a requirement, I feel like that a defined black box should have an interface... reflow2 should define black boxes (part of the functional allocation to a system) and define/enforce interface contracts (MOSA I don't think would be possible without contracts)."* He named the exceptions himself: designs with no black boxes at all, boundaries where a contract is deliberately not enforced, and a single black box with nothing to interface with.

SEARCHED FIRST, at his instruction. Read: `dec:mosa-conformance`, `req:key-interfaces` (accepted), `req:modularity-computed` (accepted), `cap:key-interfaces`, `ver:key-interfaces`, `req:interface-spec-complete`, `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`, `dec:idea-how-does-a-users-project-acquire-vocabulary-it-never-uses`, and the three interface detectors in detect.rs. **MUCH OF THIS IS ALREADY SETTLED AND BUILT** — what follows is only what is not.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ WHAT MOSA ALREADY PRODUCED HERE, so it is not re-litigated

`dec:mosa-conformance` (2026-07-25) found exactly two things missing and BOTH WERE PROMOTED THE SAME DAY on his word and are now ACCEPTED: `req:key-interfaces` — the design says which boundaries are published — and `req:modularity-computed` — severability is computed, not asserted by the diagram. `Interface.designation` (internal / published / required / both) IS the key-interface marker MOSA needed, and it is built and tested (`cap:key-interfaces`, `ver:key-interfaces`, 8 cases).

So the vocabulary half of his instinct is DONE. What is missing is checks.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📐 THE ANALOGY IS EXACT, AND MEASURED 2026-08-20 ON THIS DESIGN

  a Capability with no Requirement   → `unmotivated_capability` FIRES
  a Component with no Interface      → NOTHING FIRES

  56 Components
    14  carry any PROVIDES or CONSUMES
    42  carry none
      · 24 of those are in a DEPENDS_ON pair, so `undeclared_seam` sees them —
        but AGGREGATED into ONE project-scoped gap at severity 0.45
      · 18 are NEITHER coupled NOR interfaced: **nothing in reflow2 sees them at all**

Those 18 are the finding. They are black boxes in name only — no boundary, no coupling, nothing to sever along — and every instrument reports clean over them.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 AND THE SECOND HOLE IS WORSE, BECAUSE IT IS ON THE PUBLISHED BOUNDARIES

`req:interface-spec-complete` is ACCEPTED intent — a published contract must carry what two systems have to AGREE on, in terms a computation can compare. **NOTHING CHECKS IT.** Measured on this design:

  4 interfaces designated `published`
  3 of the 4 have unset contract fields:
     ifc:core-api        7 of 9 unset
     ifc:graph-export    6 of 9 unset
     ifc:mcp-tools-http  1 of 9 unset

reflow2 publishes a boundary whose medium, paradigm, payload format, auth and error model are all `unspecified`, and calls the design green. That is MOSA step 4 — DEFINE INTERFACES — unenforced on the tool's own published surface.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📋 MOSA'S FIVE STEPS, AGAINST WHAT REFLOW2 HAS — vocabulary vs check

  1 PLAN                    Flow/process modelling exists          check: n/a
  2 MODULARIZE              modularity computed                    check: FIXED 2026-08-20
                                                                   (it read 1.00 over nothing;
                                                                    now NOT MEASURABLE, honestly)
  3 IDENTIFY INTERFACES     `designation` built and tested         check: NONE — nothing says
                                                                   you never identified any
  4 DEFINE INTERFACES       10 structured fields, `set_interface_spec`  check: NONE — 3 of 4
                                                                   published are incomplete
  5 STANDARDIZE INTERFACES  DesignRule with `enforced` (17 rules,  check: NONE binding a rule
                            6 enforced)                            to an interface as a standard

FOUR OF FIVE HAVE THE VOCABULARY AND NO CHECK. That is the three-legs pattern (`fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`) landing on the interface layer specifically: typed tool yes, instruction yes, DETECTOR THAT NOTICES ABSENCE no.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS

**A. `uninterfaced_component` — a black box with no boundary at all.** The exact sibling of `unmotivated_capability`. Catches the 18 nothing currently sees.
   ⚠️ Noise: 42 of 56 on this design. Aggregate like `undeclared_seam` does, or per-component? Aggregation is what made the 73 uncontracted pairs read as one 0.45 note nobody acted on for months — so the aggregation that controls noise is also what buried the last finding of this shape.

**B. `incomplete_published_contract` — a boundary designated `published` with the agreement axes unset.** Directly satisfies `req:interface-spec-complete`, which is accepted and unimplemented. Narrow by construction: it fires only on what the design has already CHOSEN to publish, so it cannot nag a design that has not started.
   ⭐ Cheapest of these, most defensible, and it is the MOSA step that makes severability mean anything.

**C. Let a ruling declare the exceptions.** His three cases — no black boxes yet, contract deliberately unenforced, a single box — are DELIBERATE STATES, and `governed_by(..., ruling: "parks")` already exists for exactly that. It would need extending to these detectors, which is the same reachability problem `parks` already has.

**D. Self-limit rather than enumerate exceptions.** Precedent from 2026-08-20: `level_spine_disagreement` compares against the highest level PRESENT, so a flat design reports nothing and no ladder depth is prescribed. The same move here — fire only where the design has ALREADY used interfaces somewhere — handles "no black boxes yet" and "single box" without anyone declaring an exception.
   ⚠️ But it also means a design that never draws a single interface is never asked about it, which is `dec:idea-how-does-a-users-project-acquire-vocabulary-it-never-uses` — open, and the harder half.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ ONE PUSHBACK ON HIS OWN EXCEPTION, offered because it may sharpen the rule

He asks whether a design could have no black boxes, and treats "a single black box with nothing to interface with" as an exception. IN SE TERMS IT MAY NOT BE ONE. A system is defined by its boundary — that is what makes it a system rather than a region of the universe. A single black box still has an interface: to its ENVIRONMENT. reflow2 already supports this (an Interface may sit between a Component and an ACTOR, not only between two Components), so the vocabulary is there.

If that holds, the rule is stronger and simpler than he proposed: **every black box has at least one interface — to a sibling or to the environment — and a box with none has not been bounded yet.** The genuine exceptions then are not about EXISTENCE but about ENFORCEMENT: how complete the contract must be, and whether both sides are held to it.

⚠️ COUNTER, recorded beside it: that is an SE-domain claim, and `req:design-anything` keeps the vocabulary neutral. Whether "every element has a boundary" is a universal truth or a systems-engineering convention is exactly the kind of thing this project refuses to assume on a user's behalf.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠️ HONEST BOUNDS

· Every number here is from reflow2's own graph. Whether 42-of-56 is typical of a user's project is unknown — and by the standing rule, what this means for an arbitrary project is the question that matters, not what it means here.
· Nothing is costed. B looks small; A's noise question is unresolved and is the one that decides whether it helps or joins the 80 unsurfaced gaps.
· `dec:mosa-conformance` stays OPEN on its own narrower question — whether to ship a MOSA-BRANDED report — and nothing here decides that. Its own answer leans: a view over computations that exist, never schema, because adopting one domain's language is what reflow2 has refused since the beginning.
properties.name: OPEN — should a Component with no interface be a finding, the way a Capability with no Requirement already is? And should a PUBLISHED contract have to be complete?
